key_insight: A physics-constrained, data-driven reduced-order modeling framework enables flapping-wing shape optimization, improving time-averaged thrust by 37% and propulsive efficiency by 40%.
engineering_relevance: The approach could reduce computational and memory costs for aerodynamic design optimization involving unsteady, nonlinear flows.
method: Build physics-constrained, data-driven reduced-order models of flow dynamics.
Project PDE-constrained optimization into system dynamics optimization in Hilbert space.
Optimize wing shapes using reduced-order constraints to mitigate forward-sensitivity instability.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports 37% higher time-averaged thrust and 40% higher propulsive efficiency for a 2D flapping wing at Re = 2,400, plus a 3D demonstration.
watch_item: The abstract does not quantify 3D performance gains or establish reliability beyond the tested flow conditions.
paper_title: Aerodynamic Shape Optimization of unsteady flapping wings
